episodes.subject: aptitude
episodes.title: Percentages, ratios and interest
episodes.description: Calculate interest, changing percentages, ratios and shop prices.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, it's Maya. I've got Leo with me for Percentages, ratios and interest.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Turn everyday numbers into clear decisions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: calculate interest, changing percentages, ratios and shop prices.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with simple and compound interest and work our way to profit, loss and discount.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's start with simple and compound interest. What do we need to know?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Interest is extra money earned or paid on a principal. Simple interest uses the original principal each year. Annual compounding adds interest to the balance before the next year.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Principal means starting money.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: At 10%, ₹1,000 becomes ₹1,200 after two years with simple interest, or ₹1,210 with annual compounding.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to percentages. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A percentage is a fraction out of 100. Percentage change compares a change with the original value. Successive changes multiply because the second change acts on the new base.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Base means the whole being compared.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A library has 240 books; 25% are fiction. How many fiction books are there?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Successive percentages usually use different bases.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A ratio compares quantities using equal-sized parts. Scaling every part by the same factor preserves the ratio. Direct proportion keeps a rate constant; inverse proportion keeps a product constant under fixed-work assumptions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Ratio means relative quantities in parts.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Split 20 biscuits in the ratio 2:3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Five parts give 4 biscuits per part; the shares are 8 and 12.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Profit compares selling price with cost price. Profit and loss percentages use cost price as the base. Discounts use marked price instead. Those bases are distinct.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Cost price means the seller’s purchase cost.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A maker spends ₹250 on a lamp and sells it for ₹300. What is the profit?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave percentages, ratios and interest, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Interest is extra money earned or paid on a principal. Simple interest uses the original principal each year. Annual compounding adds interest to the balance before the next year.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Profit compares selling price with cost price. Profit and loss percentages use cost price as the base. Discounts use marked price instead. Those bases are distinct.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A useful next step is to revisit profit, loss and discount with an example of your own. Keep it small enough to check by hand.

episodes.subject: aptitude
episodes.title: Work rates, speed and divisibility
episodes.description: Combine work rates, compare journeys and decode divisibility.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome to CSQuest Audio. I'm Maya, here with Leo. This section is called Work rates, speed and divisibility.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Make rates and relationships visible.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: combine work rates, compare journeys and decode divisibility.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with time and work and work our way to number systems and divisibility.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: That takes us to time and work. Where does it fit?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Work completed equals rate times time. A worker who finishes a fixed job in d days has rate 1/d jobs per day. Independent workers’ rates add when there is no interference.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rate means work completed per time unit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A needs 6 days and B needs 3.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Their combined rate is 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 job/day; together they finish in 2 days.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Combine work rates, not completion times.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: speed and distance.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Distance equals speed times time. Units must agree. Closing speeds add for travellers moving toward each other and subtract for a faster traveller chasing another in the same direction.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Speed means distance per time unit.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A walker covers 15 km at 5 km/h. How many hours does it take?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Time = 15/5 = 3 hours.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Average speed depends on distance and time weighting.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Integers include negative whole numbers, zero and positive whole numbers. A prime is greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors. Remainders, GCD and LCM describe division and repeating patterns.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Prime means integer greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: 12 has divisors 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: For 8 and 12, GCD = 4 and LCM = 24.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave work rates, speed and divisibility, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Work completed equals rate times time. A worker who finishes a fixed job in d days has rate 1/d jobs per day. Independent workers’ rates add when there is no interference.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Integers include negative whole numbers, zero and positive whole numbers. A prime is greater than 1 with exactly two positive divisors. Remainders, GCD and LCM describe division and repeating patterns.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We've covered a lot in work rates, speed and divisibility. You don't have to remember every detail at once; start by trying one of the examples yourself.

episodes.subject: aptitude
episodes.title: Spatial reasoning, sets and arrangements
episodes.description: Explore reflections, overlapping groups, directions and arrangements.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Hi, I'm Maya. Leo's with me, and today's section is called Spatial reasoning, sets and arrangements.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rotate, arrange and reason your way through.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: explore reflections, overlapping groups, directions and arrangements.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with spatial reasoning and work our way to arrangements and data reasoning.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: There's another piece to this: spatial reasoning.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Rotation turns a shape without changing its size or handedness. Reflection reverses handedness across a mirror line. Solid-shape questions track faces and edges rather than judging a drawing by appearance alone.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Rotation means turning around a fixed centre.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An upward arrow points right after a clockwise quarter-turn.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A right-pointing arrow reflected in a vertical mirror points left.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on sets, directions and series.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A Venn diagram separates shared members from members of only one group. Direction problems combine horizontal and vertical displacements separately. A stated numerical pattern helps justify a series continuation.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Union means in at least one group.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Of 30 club members, 18 like books, 12 games and 6 both. How many like at least one?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: An arrangement must satisfy every positional clue. Data questions need correct labels, units and totals. Clock questions distinguish hand positions from elapsed time.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Constraint means a condition all valid solutions satisfy.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Asha is left of Ben, and Ben is left of Chen.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The only order is Asha → Ben → Chen.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave spatial reasoning, sets and arrangements, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Rotation turns a shape without changing its size or handedness. Reflection reverses handedness across a mirror line. Solid-shape questions track faces and edges rather than judging a drawing by appearance alone.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: An arrangement must satisfy every positional clue. Data questions need correct labels, units and totals. Clock questions distinguish hand positions from elapsed time.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Try explaining arrangements and data reasoning in your own words. If you get stuck, that chapter is a good place to listen again.

episodes.subject: aptitude
episodes.title: Absolute value, floor and ceiling
episodes.description: Use absolute value, floor and ceiling in practical scenarios.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome back. Maya here, with Leo. We've reached the section called Absolute value, floor and ceiling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Distance, boundaries and whole-number decisions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: use absolute value, floor and ceiling in practical scenarios.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with absolute value and work our way to floor and ceiling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Let's spend a moment on absolute value.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Absolute value |x| is nonnegative distance from zero. |x − a| is distance from x to a. Distance equations give points around a centre; distance inequalities describe intervals.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Absolute value means distance from zero.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: |−4| = 4. Points 3 units from 2 are −1 and 5.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Points within 3 units of 2 fill [−1, 5].

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain floor and ceiling to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Floor(x) is the greatest integer at or below x. Ceiling(x) is the smallest integer at or above x. Neither is nearest-integer rounding; negative inputs still move down for floor and up for ceiling.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Floor means integer at or below the value.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: What is ceiling(3.8)?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Four is the smallest integer no smaller than 3.8.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose 4.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: State rounding direction and check negative inputs when relevant.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave absolute value, floor and ceiling, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Absolute value |x| is nonnegative distance from zero. |x − a| is distance from x to a. Distance equations give points around a centre; distance inequalities describe intervals.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Floor(x) is the greatest integer at or below x. Ceiling(x) is the smallest integer at or above x. Neither is nearest-integer rounding; negative inputs still move down for floor and up for ceiling.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: When you try a problem on floor and ceiling, talk through why each step works. That's a useful check on what has clicked.

episodes.subject: aptitude
episodes.title: Grammar, vocabulary and logical inference
episodes.description: Build clear sentences, infer vocabulary and evaluate conclusions.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: I'm Maya, and this is CSQuest Audio. Today, Leo and I are taking on Grammar, vocabulary and logical inference.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Read closely. Connect ideas. Think clearly.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Here's what we're working toward: build clear sentences, infer vocabulary and evaluate conclusions.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: We'll begin with grammar and sentence structure and work our way to reading and critical reasoning.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: How would you explain grammar and sentence structure to someone meeting it for the first time?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A clear sentence matches a verb with its subject and uses tense to express time. Descriptive phrases do not change a main subject’s number. Meaning determines which grammatical form fits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Subject means who or what the sentence concerns.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: “The box of pencils is here” uses is for the singular box. “The pencils are here” uses are for plural pencils.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: I want to unpack vocabulary and connections next.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Context constrains a word’s meaning. Connectors show contrast, cause, sequence or addition. A chosen word must fit both the meaning and the grammar of its sentence.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Context means surrounding clues to meaning.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: “The room was sparse: it held only a chair and a table.” Sparse means…

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The few objects provide the clue.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: So we'd choose Bare or thinly furnished.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A valid reading inference follows from supplied information. Distinguish limited observations from universal claims and an association from a demonstrated cause. Avoid adding unstated facts.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Evidence means information supplied.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A museum extended Saturday hours and attendance rose.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Both occurred, but without more evidence we cannot prove the new hours caused the rise.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Before we leave grammar, vocabulary and logical inference, let's connect the pieces.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: A clear sentence matches a verb with its subject and uses tense to express time. Descriptive phrases do not change a main subject’s number. Meaning determines which grammatical form fits.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: A valid reading inference follows from supplied information. Distinguish limited observations from universal claims and an association from a demonstrated cause. Avoid adding unstated facts.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Take a small example of grammar and sentence structure and work it out before looking at the explanation. Then compare your reasoning.
